methods.label: Use the common difference
methods.explanation:
An arithmetic progression adds the same number at every step. The difference between the first two terms is
\[
(x+1)-(x-1)=2.
\]
The third term must therefore be \((x+1)+2=x+3\). Equating this with the given third term gives
\[
2x+3=x+3,
\]
so \(x=0\). Substituting gives the terms \(-1,1,3\), which do have common difference \(2\). Thus \(x=0\), choice B.
